rich_summary: As Bhishma lies on his bed of arrows after being felled, he publicly praises Arjuna’s unmatched prowess and warns Duryodhana that continuing the war will destroy the Kuru race. He urges peace while there is still time—before Bhima, Yudhishthira, and the other Pandavas annihilate the Kaurava forces—and even suggests returning half the kingdom. Duryodhana refuses the counsel, “like a dying man rejecting medicine.” Later Karna visits the wounded Bhishma. In a private, emotional exchange, Bhishma reveals he has always known Karna is Kunti’s son and praises his valor, urging him to reconcile with the Pandavas, his brothers. Karna acknowledges the truth but refuses, bound by loyalty to Duryodhana and by fate. Bhishma reluctantly grants him permission to fight. The episode closes the Bhishma Parva, emphasizing tragic loyalty, destiny, and missed chances for peace.

highlight_spans.why: Bhishma’s opening praise of Arjuna establishes his near‑divine reputation and frames the Pandava hero as unstoppable.
Bhishma’s extended warning to Duryodhana and plea for peace encapsulate the central moral theme: pride and stubbornness leading to ruin.
The early section leading into Bhishma’s final counsel captures the emotional gravity of a dying elder trying to save his family from destruction.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma, pierced by countless arrows and lying upon a bed of shafts, addresses the gathered kings while Duryodhana listens in troubled silence.
Karna approaches the fallen Bhishma at night, kneels with tears in his eyes, and the old warrior raises himself slightly to embrace him like a father.
The dying Bhishma revealing Karna’s true birth as Kunti’s son while the two warriors speak privately beside the arrow-bed.
